title: Garden Gate, Fence & Pathway Repair – Sanur Villa Guide
meta: Fix a squeaky gate, cracked pathway or leaning fence in your Sanur villa. Practical steps for small garden repairs before the rainy season hits.
intro: If your garden gate sticks after a monsoon week, a paver has cracked under the weight of a delivery van, or the fence panel by the road has started to lean, these are small jobs that snowball fast in Sanur's humidity and salt air. Most of them can be sorted with basic tools and a bit of know-how before they turn into expensive structural problems. Here is what to check, how to fix it yourself, and when it is time to call someone in.

paragraphs: Walk around your plot once a month and note anything that feels off: a hinge that no longer sits flush, a paver that rocks when you step on it, a section of fence that has pulled away from its post, an outdoor light that flickers or has a corroded fitting. In older Sanur villas the original masonry and timber were often built to a lighter spec than modern standards, so small shifts compound quickly once the sea breeze starts working on exposed metal and wood.

You do not need to be a builder to handle most of this. A set of Allen keys, a rubber mallet, a bucket of fresh sand, a tube of marine-grade grease, and a pair of work gloves cover ninety percent of the list. What you should never attempt without a licensed electrician is anything involving wiring, junction boxes, or fixtures within arm's reach of a pool.

Start at the hinges. Remove each pin, clean out old grease and rust with a wire brush, and repack with a thin layer of marine-grade lithium grease. If the gate sags and scrapes the ground, the top hinge has usually stretched; tighten the fixing bolts into the frame and, if the holes are stripped, drive in a slightly larger screw or add a washer behind the head. For wooden gates common in older Sanur properties, check that the bottom rail is still seated in its channel – a swollen board will bind after two rainy weeks.

The latch side matters just as much. A misaligned strike plate is the number-one reason a gate 'won't close.' Loosen the two screws on the strike, shift it up or down by a few millimetres so the bolt drops cleanly, and retighten. If the gate is metal and the surface is pitted from salt air, sand back to bare metal, apply a zinc-rich primer, then two coats of exterior paint before the next dry spell. Skip this and the corrosion will eat through within a season.

If the gate post itself has shifted – you can see a gap between the post and the fence line – dig around the base, pack fresh concrete or compacted gravel, and let it cure for 48 hours before hanging the gate again. Do not force the gate shut while the mix is still soft.
bullets: Grease hinges every three months; the sea breeze accelerates wear
Check the latch alignment after any storm that shakes the frame
Wooden gates: re-oil or varnish the bottom rail each dry season

paragraphs: A single cracked paver looks cosmetic until rain pools in the gap and washes out the sand bed underneath. Once the bedding layer goes, neighbouring stones start to tilt and the whole run becomes a trip hazard. Lift the affected stone with a flat pry bar, rake out the old sand, sweep the area clean, and repack with coarse river sand tamped firm. Set the paver back level with its neighbours and brush excess sand into the joints.

In Sanur the PDAM supply and rooftop tank overflow often route water across garden paths. If you notice a persistent dark streak or a patch of moss on one section, trace where the runoff lands and redirect it with a small channel drain or a sloped gravel strip before the next wet month. Left alone, standing water will crack thin concrete slabs within two rainy seasons.
bullets: Sweep and re-sand joints twice a year – before April and before November
Replace any paver that rocks more than 5 mm underfoot
Keep drainage clear so monsoon water does not undercut the path

paragraphs: Corroded lamp holders, cracked IP-rated covers, and loose cable glands are common in coastal Bali. Visually inspect every fixture: if you see green or white crust inside the socket, or the seal around the glass is split, replace the fitting rather than trying to clean it. Salt-laden moisture gets in and will short the connection within weeks.

Here is the hard rule: if the light is near your pool, spa, or any standing-water feature, stop and call a licensed electrician. Do not open the housing yourself, do not swap bulbs while the circuit is live, and do not mix any cleaning chemicals (including chlorine from pool maintenance) near an energised fitting. The combination of salt air, humidity, and water makes these circuits unforgiving. A professional can test insulation resistance and re-seal the junction properly.

The dry season (roughly April through October) is your window for painting, sealing wood, repointing masonry, and any job that needs 24–48 hours of rain-free curing. Book those tasks early in the dry run so you have buffer days before the first heavy showers arrive.

Once November rolls in and the sky turns grey by ten a.m., shift your focus to drainage: clear scupper channels off the villa roof, check that path slopes still shed water away from the gate post, and make sure no paver has shifted enough to create a puddle trap. Small fixes in the wet are harder because everything is soft and muddy; what takes twenty minutes in May can take two hours in December.

Year-round, the sea breeze does its quiet work on exposed metal. A quick visual walk-around every month – hinges, fence brackets, light fittings – catches corrosion while it is still surface-level and cheap to treat.

faq.q: My wooden gate sticks after rain but works fine when dry. Is that normal?
faq.a: A little swelling is expected in Bali's humidity, but if the gate will not close at all, the bottom rail has likely warped or the hinge screws have loosened into soft wood. Tighten the fixings, plane a millimetre off the contact edge if needed, and re-oil the rail. If the warp is more than a few millimetres, the board may need replacing – send a photo and we can advise whether it is a DIY swap or a job for a carpenter.

faq.q: How do I stop my garden path from cracking again after the monsoon?
faq.a: Cracking usually means water is pooling under the pavers because the sand bed has washed out or the slope is wrong. Re-sand the joints with coarse river sand, make sure the path falls away from the villa by at least 1–2 cm per metre, and add a small channel drain where roof runoff hits. If the sub-base is sandy soil (common on older Sanur plots), consider laying a geotextile sheet and a thin gravel layer before resetting the stones.

faq.q: Can I replace an outdoor light fitting myself near the pool?
faq.a: If the fixture is within three metres of the pool edge or any standing-water area, please do not open it yourself. Salt air plus humidity makes those circuits a genuine shock risk. Call a licensed electrician to test the insulation, replace the fitting, and re-seal the junction box. For lights well clear of water you can swap a bulb or a corroded holder, but only with the power isolated at the breaker.

cta: Not sure whether your gate, fence, or pathway needs a quick fix or a proper repair? Snap a photo in good daylight and send it over on WhatsApp – we will take a look and let you know what is involved.
